concept.learning_outcome: Identify the actual water problem before choosing treatment; understand the distinct jobs and limits of natural/material treatment methods; compare historical/global water systems by place and mechanism; investigate copper, Moringa, frequency and lunar-human questions with appropriate evidence boundaries; transfer diagnostic and evidence-literacy principles elsewhere.
concept.central_question: What is the water problem, what can each method actually do, and what evidence shows the claim is the right size?
major_principles: Clear water is not automatically safe water.
Diagnose before prescribing; match treatment to the actual contaminant/problem.
Water treatment is a chain, not a magic ingredient.
Source protection is part of treatment.
Traditional and modern describe context, not truth value.
Local source, climate, fuel, materials and infrastructure shape water systems.
A real mechanism does not make a method universal.
Match the claim to the mechanism and evidence.
Observation, mechanism, persistence, replication, biological effect, health effect and recommendation are different levels of claim.
Prove only what the evidence proves.
concept.historical_or_lost_knowledge_angle: Preserve the original whole-household/source-protection water-system teaching, then expand it with named global practices and laboratory testing of traditional methods.
concept.current_use_angle: Use filtration, source protection, copper, Moringa, acoustics/frequency and lunar-human research to teach practical water knowledge and evidence literacy.
concept.transfer_the_principle_summary: Both transferable principles are preserved separately: Diagnose before prescribing / match the solution to the actual problem; and match the claim to the mechanism and evidence.
